newsitem.title: ITALY: Anglican is ordained as first woman priest in Rome.
newsitem.headline: Anglican is ordained as first woman priest in Rome.

text.p: A 43-year-old Anglican has become the first woman to be ordained as a priest in Rome, the capital of Roman Catholicism, unleashing a torrent of interest in Italy.

Cecilia Monge Teran de Erazo, a grandmother whose husband Juan is also a priest and who converted from Catholicism in the 1980s, was ordained last Sunday at the American Episcopal Church of Saint Paul's Within-the-Walls.
The couple, who are both from Ecuador, will celebrate their first public mass together next Sunday, a spokeswoman at the church said on Tuesday.

"We wanted to keep it (the ordination) as quiet as possible but the press found out and it has kind of snowballed from then on. Cecilia was a bit surprised that people were so interested," the spokeswoman said.
The Vatican, which flatly rejects the notion of women as priests, had no immediate comment on the ordination.
It has in the past made clear that it regards the ordination of women priests by churches of the Anglican Communion, of which the Episcopal Church is part, as an obstacle to Christian unity.

Religious sources say Pope John Paul is expected to meet the Archbishop of Canterbury, Dr George Carey, at the Vatican in December for talks that are certain to tackle divisions over the position of women in religious life.
Carey's Church of England is the mother church of the Anglican Communion, which has some 80 million members worldwide.

"I certainly do know (about the differences about women priests) and I am sorry about them but I am happy that in my church there is this possibility," Corriere della Sera newspaper quoted Monge as saying on Tuesday.
"Imagine how beautiful it is to be a priest and married to a priest," she said.
Monge, who has three children and two grandchildren, moved to Rome five years ago with her husband to help with pastoral work for Latin American immigrants.
She said she had served for several years as a deacon before deciding five months ago to become a priest.
"I have always wanted to be a servant of the Lord and when I was a Catholic I thought of becoming a nun but my father was against it and I couldn't," she said.
"I have good memories (of the Catholic Church), where I was baptised, married and where two of our children were baptised.
"I wouldn't take anything away from it but it's true that I feel better in this church which I embraced later on," the newspaper quoted her as saying.
